facts.text: Mausoleum complex of Zhu Yuanzhang, the Hongwu Emperor who founded the Ming dynasty, at the southern foot of Purple Mountain.
A sacred way (shendao) about a mile long runs from the Square Pavilion with its giant bixi turtle to the burial mound, lined with stone camels and elephants.
Legend says 13 identical funeral processions left 13 city gates to hide the real burial site.

facts.text: Memorial to the victims of the 1937 Nanjing Massacre, with two partly excavated mass-burial sites, sculptures and a museum.
Captions are in English, Chinese and Japanese; entry is free and queues can be long.

facts.text: Former seat of the Republic of China presidency from 1927 to 1949, now the China Modern History Museum, at 292 Changjiang Road.
Includes the former offices of Chiang Kai-shek and Sun Yat-sen; ticket requires showing a passport.

facts.text: Highest hill in Nanjing at 448.9 m, on the eastern side of the city, named for purple and golden clouds at dawn and dusk.
Home to the tombs of Sun Yat-sen, the Hongwu Emperor and Sun Quan; a shuttle train and cable car (Y25 one way) run on the mountain.
Entry to the park needs a free reservation (WeChat or passport at tourist information centres); individual sights charge their own fees.

facts.text: Southern gate of the Nanjing city wall, a complex defensive gate described as one of the best preserved in the world.
Interior depots hold models and exhibits; the courtyards include an archery range.

facts.text: Chinese garden beside the Confucius Temple at 128 Zhan Yuan Road, first built in the early Ming by the general Xu Da.
Rebuilt after the Taiping Rebellion; the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom History Museum stands in the grounds.

Wikivoyage calls it the most popular temple in Nanjing, convenient to downtown.

facts.text: Double-deck road-rail bridge across the Yangtze joining Pukou and Gulou districts, with a 4,588 m road deck.
Carries classic socialist-art sculptures of workers, farmers and soldiers; the first major Yangtze bridge built without foreign help.

facts.text: Mountain in the northeast of Nanjing's Qixia District, site of Qixia Temple and known for autumn maples.
Network of trails links pavilions, stone formations and a canyon; best in autumn maples or spring peach blossom.
